title: One valley, properly
standfirst: Four hours from Delhi and a world away, provided you stay in one valley rather than touring three.

blocks.heading: Walks from the door
paras: Himachal's valleys are close together on a map and separated by long, winding drives in practice.
We put members in one valley for the week, in a house with walks from the door rather than drives to trailheads.

blocks.heading: Tea and deodar
blocks.caption: Tea-estate bungalows below the first ridge.
paras: The tea country below Dharamshala is quieter than the hill stations and the bungalows are old, large and privately run.
They take one party at a time, with a cook who shops the local market each morning.

blocks.heading: The ridge above
blocks.caption: The snow line is a morning's walk, not an expedition.
paras: The first real Himalayan ridge is a few hours above the valley floor and needs no technical skill at all.
A guide and an early start is the whole requirement, and the view at the top is the one people fly to Nepal for.

blocks.heading: Questions members ask
blocks.intro: The ones that come up nearly every time.

a: March to June and September to November. The monsoon closes the high valleys and winter closes the passes.
Fly to the valley airstrip where weather allows, or drive from Delhi. We hold both and decide the day before.
Five to seven nights in one valley. Longer if a second valley is genuinely wanted.

blocks.heading: We are ready when you are
paras: Every itinerary starts with a conversation about what you actually want from the days, and works backwards to houses, guides and timing from there.
